chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrifices of the Christian Arabs, whether they are permissible to eat? He said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to prohibit eating their sacrifices and their game. He said: A Jew or a Christian should not slaughter your Udhiyah (sacrificial animal).

key_terms.الذَّبَائِحِ: Sacrifices (animals slaughtered for food or ritual)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of sacrifices from Christian Arabs permissible to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the juristic status of Christian Arab sacrifices by linking them to the precedent of Imam Ali (AS), who prohibited their consumption, thereby establishing a distinct ruling for 'Ahl al-Kitab' of the Arab tribes. It further specifies that a Jew or Christian is invalid as a slaughterer for one's own Udhiyah, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the religious identity of the slaughterer in ensuring the meat's purity and validity for consumption.
